factual_claims.claim: AI systems are being rapidly integrated into critical infrastructure, financial systems, healthcare, and defense applications.
Traditional cybersecurity frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK are inadequate for addressing AI-specific vulnerabilities.
AI systems introduce novel categories of vulnerabilities, such as training data poisoning and human feedback exploitation, that are absent in traditional software.
AI agents can autonomously perform multi-step tasks such as browsing the web, writing code, and executing system commands.
Autonomous AI agents operating at machine speed can cause cascading real-world failures before human operators can intervene.
Current AI systems are susceptible to prompt injection and adversarial manipulation that bypasses safety filters.
AI agents can be manipulated to perform autonomous replication and spread across networks.
Current AI guardrail systems are fragile and can be bypassed by techniques like emoji smuggling and policy puppetry.
AI agents can execute thousands of requests per second, necessitating automated detection and containment.
Only 250 poisoned documents are needed to backdoor any model regardless of size.
